title: Sparrowhook — micro-feature inklings notebook
content:
Context / one-line idea:
Sparrowhook = a collection of tiny, contextual onboarding nudges ('inklings') that appear where a user is about to hit high cost/uncertainty or a low-success surface. Goal is to reduce time-to-first-success and lower support friction by surfacing a short, actionable micro-flow (1–3 steps) instead of a full doc or page redirect.

Why this?
- We see new-hosted API users often get stuck at: creating prompt templates, picking batching/quantization settings, and picking model variants for cost tradeoffs.
- Full PRDs + big tours are heavy; small inline affordances might convert more quickly.
- Fits developer-first ethos: short, contextual, power-user skippable.

Examples / vignettes (user stories):
1) New dev: "I want a quick success — send a minimal prompt and see a generated response."
   - Inklings: small "Try a sample prompt" widget prefilled, single-click run, shows tokens & cost estimate under the hood.
   - Acceptance: user runs sample within 30s, sees result, and clicks "Save as template" or "Use in project".

2) Team lead evaluating Dedicated: "I need to know latency/cost implication for my routes."
   - Inklings: on the model selection dropdown, show a lightweight inline comparison (median latency / estimated token cost / recommended fixture) with a CTA "Profile this route".

3) Returning user with churn risk: "My recent runs went up in cost"
   - Inklings: small banner on dashboard: "We noticed cost drift on route X — try 'Cost-saver' config" with one-click apply to create a canary with lower precision.

Core hypotheses:
- H1: Including an inline runnable sample will increase time-to-first-success (deploy or template-save) from new signups by at least 25%.
- H2: Lightweight, route-level nudges will reduce support tickets about 'which model to pick' by 30% in the first 90 days.

MVP scope (90 day):
- 3 inklings: sample-prompt run widget (API quick-run), model-compare tooltip (cost/latency estimates), cost-drift banner (dashboard).
- Server-side: small profiling endpoint to return quick median latency & token-cost estimate given model + seq len distribution (budgeted, cached).
- Client-side: ephemeral UI components behind feature-flag + A/B experiment hook.
- Telemetry: impressions, clicks, run_success, follow_through (save template / apply config), retention delta.

Detailed requirements (rough):
- Frontend: lightweight component library pieces (tiny code sandbox), minimal DOM footprint, accessible, keyboard friendly.
- API contract: /profile/inkling?model=santa-v1&route=abc should return stringified estimate + variance + small sample requestId. Response must be <= 150ms p95.
- Auth: inklings should only display actions available to the current user (e.g., read-only viewers see example but not 'apply').
- Rate limit: profile endpoint should be rate-limited per-session; cache results for 10 minutes.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Sample-run inklings produce a valid model response within 2s for short prompts in 80% of runs on hosted infra.
- Model comparison tooltip appears for 90% of users on model selection flow (when feature is on).
- Cost-drift banner triggers only on >20% week-over-week cost increase or >30% token count changes to avoid noise.

Instrumentation / metrics to track:
- Activation funnel: inkling_impression -> inkling_click -> run_success -> save_template/apply_config
- Time-to-first-success (TTFS) for new signups (compare treatment vs control).
- Support deltas: tickets tagged 'model-selection' pre/post experiment.
- Engagement: repeat use of inklings per user/week.

Experiment design:
- Randomized at account level. N target: 1500 new accounts for 6 weeks to get signal on TTFS.
- Secondary: Bolt-on pilot on 50 existing mid-size accounts (sales-assisted) to test Dedicated routing tips.

UI sketch notes (very rough):
- Sample-prompt widget: small pill near top-right of quickstart panel with label: "Run a sample" -> opens inline modal with 1 text area, run button, results box, 'Save as template' CTA.
- Model compare: small chevron next to model label. Hover shows 3 rows: Model name | est cost / 1k tokens | median latency | recommended for 'short', 'balanced', 'long'.
- Cost banner: compact CTA "Apply Cost-saver" + tiny 'Explain' chevron that expands to a 2-line why (quantization, batching suggestions).

Open questions / risks:
- Data freshness: where do we get latency estimates? If we rely on historical runs, cold models/regions will be off. Need fast synthetic microprofile.
- Signal noise: too many banners/inklings = irritation. Add throttle + suppression heuristics per-user.
- Security: small runnable sample executes on hosted infra; must ensure tenant isolation and limit exposure to expensive models. Consider sandboxing and ephemeral token.
- Legal/privacy: saved templates might include PII; ensure 'Save as template' warns or strips.

Technical approach options for profile endpoint:
A) Lightweight synthetic cold-call: spin a tiny request on a cheap shim service to get a timing + token estimation (higher accuracy but has cost).
B) Historical extrapolation: use recent route traces to compute median latency for token buckets. Cheap but inaccurate for new routes/models.
C) Hybrid: use history if exists else fall back to single-sample micro-call (with rate-limit).
Preference: C.

Rollout plan / safety:
- Feature-flag gated per-org; default off for enterprise customers until privacy review.
- Start with 1% of new signups -> ramp to 25% -> full.
- Canary: only show 'apply' for non-production orgs at first (or behind a permission).

Dependencies / stakeholders:
- Infra: microprofile endpoint + routing rules (infra-eng).
- Frontend: quickstart + dashboard teams (devex + console).
- Product: hosted-api PM (me) + analytics to define metrics + CS for pilot outreach.
- Legal and Trust for template-save flow.

Backlog tickets / next steps (owner initials in parens):
- PROTO-1: design sample-run UX (MB)
- PROTO-2: infra microprofile prototype (KM)
- PROTO-3: analytics instrumentation spec (LP)
- PROTO-4: suppression heuristics + UX (AR)
- PROTO-5: privacy review for saved templates (legal)

Quick experiment checklist (for initial pilot):
- [ ] Define treatment & control account lists
- [ ] Implement inkling impressions & click events with event ids
- [ ] Create simple dashboard: TTFS, funnel conversion, support ticket count
- [ ] Run 4-week pilot, collect qualitative feedback (CS)

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Keep inklings tiny. If a user needs a multi-step flow, redirect to a small modal 'guided setup' (separate).
- Use 'explain' links to teach users about unit economics (important trust lever).
- Consider 'developer mode' toggle so power users can mute all inklings.
- If successful, add SDK helpers so customers can opt-in and author their own inklings for internal teams.

End — want to push a tiny prototype to staging this sprint. Next sync: Wed 10am with KM, LP to scope infra cost and ETA.

- KM: feasibility note for microprofile + rough cost estimate
- LP: analytics event schema draft
